name: Can custom cabinetry be built around uneven walls in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: How do cabinet makers handle walls that are out of square, floors that slope, or ceilings that are not level?
mainEntity.text: How do cabinet makers handle walls that are out of square, floors that slope, or ceilings that are not level?

acceptedAnswer.text: Uneven walls and floors are common in older Los Angeles homes, especially in neighborhoods with original construction or multiple remodel phases. Custom cabinetry is designed for this problem because each cabinet can be built and fitted to actual site conditions rather than standard dimensions. Installers typically measure after framing, drywall, and flooring are stable, then use shims, scribing, fillers, and custom end panels to create a clean fit. The important part is that the design allows for these adjustments from the beginning. If cabinet dimensions are too rigid, the final result may include awkward gaps or forced compromises. Before fabrication, confirm where the walls are out of square, where appliances need extra clearance, and whether crown or base trim will be integrated. A good cabinet maker treats site irregularity as a normal part of the process, not a defect.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Custom cabinetry is often the best solution for older homes because cabinets can be scribed, shimmed, and trimmed to fit uneven walls and sloped floors. The installer measures the site carefully, then adjusts end panels, fillers, and toe-kicks for a tight fit. Proper planning prevents gaps and visible misalignment.
